title.zh: 卷一百十二 列傳第四十二: 逆臣上
title.raw: 卷一百十二 列傳第四十二: 逆臣上 Volume 112 Biographies 42: Rebellious Officials 1

sentences.zh: 逆臣上

translations.literal: Rebellious Ministers, Upper Part
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Officials, Part One

sentences.zh: ○耶律轄底

translations.literal: ○ Yelü Xiadǐ
translations.idiomatic: • Yelü Xiadǐ

sentences.zh: 〈（叠裏特）〉

translations.literal: (Dialite)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Dialite)]〉

sentences.zh: 耶律察割耶律婁國耶律重元

translations.literal: Yelü Chaguo, Yelü Louguo, Yelü Chongyuan
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Chaguo, Yelü Louguo, and Yelü Chongyuan

sentences.zh: 〈（涅魯古）〉

translations.literal: (Nielugu)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Nielugu)]〉

sentences.zh: 耶律滑哥

translations.literal: Yelü Huage
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Huage

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天尊地卑，乾坤定矣；

translations.literal: The 《Book of Changes》 says: "Heaven is honored and earth is base; thereby Qian and Kun are fixed;
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Changes》 says: "Heaven is honored and earth is lowly; thereby Qian and Kun are set in place;

sentences.zh: 卑高以陳，貴賤位矣。」

translations.literal: The low and the high are set forth, and the noble and the base take their places."
translations.idiomatic: Low and high are arrayed in order, and the noble and the base assume their stations."

sentences.zh: 貴賤位而後君臣之分定，君臣之分定而後天地和，天地和而後萬化成。

translations.literal: When noble and base have taken their places, then the division between lord and minister is fixed; when lord and minister are fixed, then heaven and earth are in harmony; when heaven and earth are in harmony, then the myriad things are transformed and completed.
translations.idiomatic: Once noble and base have assumed their stations, the distinction between ruler and minister is settled; once ruler and minister are settled, heaven and earth come into harmony; once heaven and earth are in harmony, the myriad things are formed and fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 五帝三王之治，用此道也。

translations.literal: The governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings employed this Way.
translations.idiomatic: The rule of the Five Emperors and Three Kings rested on this principle.

sentences.zh: 三代而降，臣弒其君者有之，子弒其父者有之。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward, there have been those in whom ministers murdered their lords, and sons murdered their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties, ministers have murdered their rulers, and sons have murdered their fathers.

sentences.zh: 孔子作《春秋》以寓王法，誅死者於前，懼生者於後，其慮深遠矣。

translations.literal: Confucius composed the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 to embody the royal law, punishing the dead before the eyes of all to frighten the living who came after—a consideration whose depth is far-reaching indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius wrote the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 to embody the kingly law, condemning the dead before all eyes to warn the living who followed—a design whose reach was profoundly far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修作《唐書》，創《逆臣傳》，蓋亦《春秋》之意也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu composed the 《Book of Tang》 and created the 《Biographies of Rebellious Ministers》, which likewise embodies the intent of the 《Spring and Autumn》.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xiu compiled the 《Book of Tang》, he inaugurated the 《Biographies of Rebellious Ministers》—surely in the same spirit as the 《Spring and Autumn》.

sentences.zh: 遼叛逆之臣二十有二，跡其事則又有甚焉者，然豈一朝一夕之故哉。

translations.literal: Liao has twenty-two ministers who rebelled, and when one traces their deeds there are those who went even further still; yet this was surely no affair of a single morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Liao counts twenty-two rebellious ministers, and tracing their deeds one finds cases still worse—yet such outcomes are never the work of a single day or night alone.

sentences.zh: 列於《傳》，所以公天下之貶，以示夫戒雲。

translations.literal: To set them forth in the 《Biographies》 is to make a public condemnation under Heaven and to offer a warning.
translations.idiomatic: They are recorded in the 《Biographies》 so that condemnation may be made public under Heaven and a warning set forth for all.

sentences.zh: 轄底，字涅烈袞，肅祖孫夷離堇怗剌之子。

translations.literal: Xiadǐ, courtesy name Nieliegun, was the son of the ürün chijin Dila, descendant of Emperor Suzu of the Yaonian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiadǐ, whose style name was Nieliegun, was the son of Dila, ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe and a descendant of the dynastic founder Suzu.

sentences.zh: 幼黠而辯，時險佞者多附之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and eloquent, and at the time many treacherous flatterers attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was sharp-witted and quick of tongue, and many crafty sycophants of the day rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 遙輦痕德堇可汗時，異母兄罨古只為叠剌部夷離堇。

translations.literal: In the time of Khan Hendejin of the Yaolian, his elder half-brother Angu'zhi was ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Khan Hendejin of the Yaolian line, his elder half-brother Angu'zhi served as ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.

sentences.zh: 故事，為夷離堇者，得行再生禮。

translations.literal: By precedent, one who became ürün chijin was permitted to perform the ritual of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, whoever assumed the office of ürün chijin was entitled to perform the rebirth ceremony.

sentences.zh: 罨古只方就帳易服，轄底遂取紅袍、貂蟬冠，乘白馬而出。

translations.literal: Angu'zhi had just entered the tent to change his garments when Xiadǐ took a red robe and sable cicada cap, mounted a white horse, and rode out.
translations.idiomatic: While Angu'zhi was still in his tent changing clothes, Xiadǐ seized a red robe and a sable cicada cap, mounted a white horse, and rode forth.

sentences.zh: 乃令黨人大呼曰：「夷離堇出矣！」

translations.literal: He then had his faction shout aloud: "The ürün chijin has come forth!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his partisans to cry out: "The ürün chijin has emerged!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆羅拜，因行柴冊禮，自立為夷離堇。

translations.literal: All bowed down in ranks, whereupon he performed the chice ritual and installed himself as ürün chijin.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd prostrated themselves in ranks; he then performed the chice ritual of investiture and declared himself ürün chijin.

sentences.zh: 與於越耶律釋魯同知國政。

translations.literal: Together with the yuyue Yelü Shilu he jointly administered state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He shared governance of the realm with Yelü Shilu, who held the honorary title of yuyue.

sentences.zh: 及釋魯遇害，轄底懼人圖己，挈其二子叠裏特、朔刮奔渤海，偽為失明。

translations.literal: When Shilu met with violence, Xiadǐ feared that others would plot against him; he took his two sons Dialite and Shuogua and fled to Bohai, feigning blindness.
translations.idiomatic: After Shilu was killed, Xiadǐ feared others would plot against him; he fled to Bohai with his sons Dialite and Shuogua and pretended to be blind.

sentences.zh: 後因球馬之會，與二子奪良馬奔歸國。

translations.literal: Later, at a ball-and-horse gathering, he and his two sons seized fine horses and galloped back to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a ball-game meeting, he and his two sons seized fine horses and raced back to the Khitan realm.

sentences.zh: 益為奸惡，常以巧辭獲免。

translations.literal: He grew ever more treacherous and wicked, yet often escaped punishment through clever words.
translations.idiomatic: He grew still more wicked, yet time and again talked his way out of punishment with clever speeches.

sentences.zh: 太祖將即位，讓轄底，轄底曰：「皇帝聖人，由天所命，臣豈敢當！」

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor was about to take the throne, he offered it to Xiadǐ; Xiadǐ said: "The emperor is a sage appointed by Heaven—how dare your subject presume to accept!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu was about to ascend the throne, he offered the realm to Xiadǐ; Xiadǐ replied, "The Son of Heaven is a sage ordained by Heaven—how could a subject such as I dare accept it!"

sentences.zh: 太祖命為於越。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor appointed him yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed him yuyue.

sentences.zh: 及自將伐西南諸部，轄底誘剌葛等亂，不從者殺之。

translations.literal: When he personally led a campaign against the tribes of the southwest, Xiadǐ incited Cige and others to rebel; those who would not follow he killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor led troops in person against the southwestern tribes, Xiadǐ incited Cige and others to revolt and killed those who refused to join.

sentences.zh: 車駕還至赤水城，轄底懼，與剌葛俱北走，至榆河，為追兵所獲。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Chishui City, Xiadǐ grew afraid; he fled north together with Cige, reached the Yu River, and was captured by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned to Chishui City, Xiadǐ took fright and fled north with Cige; at the Yu River they were overtaken and captured.

sentences.zh: 太祖問曰：「朕初即位，嘗以國讓，叔父辭之；

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor asked: "When I first took the throne I once offered you the realm, and Uncle declined it;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu asked, "When I first took the throne I offered you the realm, and you, Uncle, declined it;

sentences.zh: 今反欲立吾弟，何也？」

translations.literal: why now do you wish instead to set up my younger brother?"
translations.idiomatic: why do you now seek to set up my younger brother instead?"

sentences.zh: 轄底對曰：「始臣不知天子之貴，及陛下即位，衛從甚嚴，與凡庶不同，臣嘗奏事心動，始有窺覦之意。

translations.literal: Xiadǐ replied: "At first your subject did not know the exalted status of the Son of Heaven; after Your Majesty took the throne, your guards and attendants were exceedingly strict and unlike those of ordinary folk. When I once presented a memorial my heart was stirred, and only then did I begin to harbor designs of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiadǐ answered, "At first I did not grasp how exalted the Son of Heaven was. After Your Majesty took the throne, your escort was so strict and so unlike that of common men that when I once presented a memorial my heart stirred, and only then did I begin to covet the throne.

sentences.zh: 度陛下英武，必不可取；

translations.literal: I judged Your Majesty to be heroic and martial and surely impossible to seize;
translations.idiomatic: I judged that Your Majesty was heroic and martial and could never be overthrown;

sentences.zh: 諸弟懦弱，得則易圖也。

translations.literal: your younger brothers were weak and timid—if one obtained the throne, he would be easy to plot against.
translations.idiomatic: your younger brothers were weak—once one of them held power, he would be easy to overthrow.

sentences.zh: 事若成，豈容諸弟乎！」

translations.literal: If the affair succeeded, how could I have tolerated those younger brothers!"
translations.idiomatic: Had the plot succeeded, would I have spared your brothers!"

sentences.zh: 太祖謂諸弟曰：「汝輩乃從斯人之言耶！」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor said to his younger brothers: "You actually followed this man's words!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his brothers, "You actually listened to this man!"

sentences.zh: 叠剌曰：「謀大事者，須用如此人；

translations.literal: Yaonian said: "One who plots a great undertaking must employ men such as this;
translations.idiomatic: Yaonian replied, "Great undertakings require men like him;

sentences.zh: 事成亦必去之。」

translations.literal: when the affair succeeds, he must surely be removed."
translations.idiomatic: once the deed is done, he must certainly be removed."

sentences.zh: 轄底不復對。

translations.literal: Xiadǐ made no further reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xiadǐ said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 囚數月，縊殺之。

translations.literal: After several months in prison he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: After months in confinement he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 將刑，太祖謂曰：「叔父罪當死，朕不敢赦。

translations.literal: When he was about to be executed, the Taizu Emperor said to him: "Uncle's crime merits death, and I dare not pardon it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the execution, Emperor Taizu said, "Uncle, your crime deserves death, and I dare not pardon you.

sentences.zh: 事有便國者，宜悉言之。」

translations.literal: If there is anything that would benefit the state, you should speak of it fully."
translations.idiomatic: If anything would serve the realm, speak of it fully."

sentences.zh: 轄底曰：「叠剌部人眾勢強，故多為亂，宜分為二，以弱其勢。」

translations.literal: Xiadǐ said: "The Yaonian tribe is numerous and powerful, and for this reason it often breeds rebellion; it should be divided in two to weaken its strength."
translations.idiomatic: Xiadǐ said, "The Yaonian tribe is large and strong, which is why it so often rebels; divide it in two to weaken its power."

sentences.zh: 子叠裏特。

translations.literal: His son Dialite.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Dialite.

sentences.zh: 叠裏特，字海鄰。

translations.literal: Dialite, courtesy name Hailin.
translations.idiomatic: Dialite, whose style name was Hailin.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善馳射，馬躓不仆。

translations.literal: He possessed great physical strength, excelled at mounted archery, and when his horse stumbled would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: He was powerfully built and skilled at mounted archery; even when his horse stumbled he would not be thrown.

sentences.zh: 尤神於醫，視人疾，若隔紗睹物，莫不悉見。

translations.literal: He was especially miraculous in medicine; when he examined a person's illness it was as if he viewed objects through gauze—nothing escaped his sight.
translations.idiomatic: He was uncannily gifted in medicine; when he examined an illness it was as though he saw through a veil—nothing was hidden from him.

sentences.zh: 太祖在潛，已加眷遇，及即位，拜叠剌部夷離堇。

translations.literal: While the Taizu Emperor was still in the background, he had already shown him special favor; upon taking the throne he appointed him ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Even before Taizu took the throne he had favored Dialite; once enthroned, he appointed him ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗思鹿醢解酲，以山林所有，問能取者。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor once longed for pickled deer to sober his wine; since it was to be found in the mountains and forests, he asked who could obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once craved pickled deer to clear his head after drinking; as it could be found in the hills, he asked who could fetch it.

sentences.zh: 叠裏特曰：「臣能得之。」

translations.literal: Dialite said: "Your subject can obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: Dialite said, "I can get it."

sentences.zh: 乘內廄馬逐鹿，射其一。

translations.literal: He mounted an imperial stable horse to pursue deer and shot one.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted a horse from the imperial stables, chased deer, and brought one down with a shot.

sentences.zh: 欲復射，馬跌而斃。

translations.literal: As he was about to shoot again, the horse stumbled and died.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared a second shot, the horse stumbled and fell dead.

sentences.zh: 叠裏特躍而前，弓猶不弛，復獲其一。

translations.literal: Dialite leaped forward, his bow still unslackened, and took another.
translations.idiomatic: Dialite sprang forward without slackening his bow and took another deer.

sentences.zh: 帝歡甚曰：「吾弟萬人敵！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "My brother is a match for ten thousand men!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and exclaimed, "My brother is a match for ten thousand men!"

sentences.zh: 會帝患心痛，召叠裏特視之。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor suffered heart pain and summoned Dialite to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor suffered heart pain, he summoned Dialite to examine him.

sentences.zh: 叠裏特曰：「膏肓有瘀血如彈丸，然藥不能及，必針而後愈。」

translations.literal: Dialite said: "In the region of the vitals there is congealed blood like a pellet, yet medicine cannot reach it; only needling will bring recovery."
translations.idiomatic: Dialite said, "There is congealed blood the size of a pellet in the deepest recesses of the chest; medicine cannot reach it—only acupuncture will cure you."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘔出瘀血，痛止。

translations.literal: He vomited forth the congealed blood and the pain ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He vomited the clotted blood and the pain stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝以其親，每加賜賚；

translations.literal: Because he was a kinsman, the emperor repeatedly bestowed gifts upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Because he was kin, the emperor showered him with gifts;

sentences.zh: 然知其為人，未嘗任以職。

translations.literal: yet knowing his character, he never entrusted him with office.
translations.idiomatic: yet knowing his character, he never gave him real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 後從剌葛亂，與其父轄底俱縊殺之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Cige in rebellion and was strangled to death together with his father Xiadǐ.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Cige's rebellion and was strangled along with his father Xiadǐ.

sentences.zh: 察割，字歐辛，明王安端之子。

translations.literal: Chaguo, courtesy name Ouxin, was the son of Prince Ming'an Anduan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo, whose style name was Ouxin, was the son of Prince Ming'an Anduan.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: He excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 貌恭而心狡，人以為懦。

translations.literal: In appearance he was deferential but in heart crafty; people took him for timid.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was respectful but his heart was cunning, and people mistook him for a coward.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此凶頑，非懦也。」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor said: "This man is fierce and obstinate—not timid."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "He is vicious and stubborn—not timid at all."

sentences.zh: 其父安端嘗使奏事，太祖謂近侍曰：「此子目若風駝，面有反相。

translations.literal: His father Anduan once sent him to present a memorial; the Taizu Emperor said to his close attendants: "This man's eyes are like those of a camel in the wind, and his face bears the marks of a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Once when his father sent him to report at court, Taizu told his attendants, "This man's eyes are like a camel's in a gale, and his face bears the look of a rebel.

sentences.zh: 朕若獨居，無令入門。」

translations.literal: If I am alone, do not let him enter the gate."
translations.idiomatic: If I am alone, do not let him through the door."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位於鎮陽，安端聞之，欲持兩端。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, Anduan heard of it and wished to keep to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, Anduan heard the news and tried to hedge between the rivals.

sentences.zh: 察割曰：「太弟忌刻，若果立，豈容我輩！

translations.literal: Chaguo said: "The Imperial Younger Brother is jealous and harsh; if he truly takes the throne, how could he tolerate us!
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo said, "The Imperial Younger Brother is jealous and cruel; if he really becomes emperor, he will never spare us!

sentences.zh: 永康王寬厚，且與劉哥相善，宜往與計。」

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang is generous and moreover on good terms with Liu Ge; we should go and consult with him."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang is generous and friendly with Liu Ge—we should go consult with them."

sentences.zh: 安端即與劉哥謀歸世宗。

translations.literal: Anduan thereupon plotted with Liu Ge to submit to Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Anduan then joined Liu Ge in plotting to submit to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，以功封泰寧王。

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was concluded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taining for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taining for his service.

sentences.zh: 會安端為西南面大詳穩，察割佯為父惡，陰遣人白於帝，即召之。

translations.literal: It happened that Anduan became Grand Commander of the Southwest; Chaguo pretended to denounce his father and secretly sent someone to report to the emperor, who immediately summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Anduan became Grand Commander of the Southwest, Chaguo pretended to denounce his father and secretly informed the emperor, who summoned him at once.

sentences.zh: 既至上前，泣訴不勝哀，帝憫之，使領女石烈軍。

translations.literal: When he came before the throne he wept and pleaded with overwhelming grief; the emperor pitied him and had him command the Nüshilie army.
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne he wept as though overcome with grief; the emperor took pity on him and put him in command of the Nüshilie army.

sentences.zh: 出入禁中，數被恩遇。

translations.literal: He went in and out of the inner palace and was repeatedly shown favor.
translations.idiomatic: He moved freely within the inner palace and was favored again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝每出獵，察割托手疾，不操弓矢，但執煉錘馳走。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out hunting, Chaguo pleaded hand ailment, did not take bow and arrow, but only grasped a forged mace and galloped about.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor hunted, Chaguo claimed a hand ailment, carried no bow, and rode about gripping only a forged mace.

sentences.zh: 屢以家之細事聞於上，上以為誠。

translations.literal: He repeatedly reported petty household matters to the throne, and the emperor took this for sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported trifling household matters to the emperor, who took this as proof of sincerity.

sentences.zh: 察割以諸族屬雜處，不克以逞，漸徙廬帳迫於行宮。

translations.literal: Because the clans of his kin were intermingled and he could not carry out his designs, he gradually moved his tents closer to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Because his kinsmen's camps were scattered and he could not act freely, he gradually moved his tents nearer the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 右皮室詳穩耶律屋質察其奸邪，表列其狀。

translations.literal: Yelü Wuzhi, Commander of the Right Pishi, perceived his treachery and submitted a memorial detailing his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wuzhi, commander of the Right Pishi, detected his treachery and memorialized the emperor with a full account.

sentences.zh: 帝不信，以表示察割。

translations.literal: The emperor did not believe it and showed the memorial to Chaguo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to believe it and showed the memorial to Chaguo.

sentences.zh: 察割稱屋質疾己，哽咽流涕。

translations.literal: Chaguo said that Wuzhi bore him ill will and choked with sobs, tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo said Wuzhi bore him a grudge and broke into choking sobs.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕固知無此，何至泣耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have always known this is not so—why go so far as to weep!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have never believed this—why weep over it!"

sentences.zh: 察割時出怨言，屋質曰：「汝雖無是心，因我過疑汝，勿為非義可也。」

translations.literal: Chaguo would from time to time utter resentful words; Wuzhi said: "Though you may not harbor such intent, because of my excess in suspecting you, do not commit wrongdoing—that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo sometimes muttered complaints; Wuzhi told him, "Even if you mean no harm, my suspicions have put you under a cloud—do not do anything improper."

sentences.zh: 他日屋質又請於帝，帝曰：「察割舍父事我，可保無他。」

translations.literal: On another day Wuzhi again petitioned the emperor; the emperor said: "Chaguo abandoned his father to serve me—he can be trusted to have no other designs."
translations.idiomatic: Another day Wuzhi pleaded again; the emperor said, "Chaguo turned against his father to serve me—he can be trusted."

sentences.zh: 屋質曰：「察割於父既不孝，於君安能忠！」

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "If Chaguo was not filial toward his father, how toward his lord can he be loyal!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi replied, "A man unfilial to his father cannot be loyal to his lord!"

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor would not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 天祿五年七月，帝幸太液谷，留飲三日，察割謀亂不果。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Tianlu, the emperor visited Taiye Valley and remained drinking for three days; Chaguo plotted rebellion but it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianlu 5, the emperor visited Taiye Valley and lingered there drinking for three days; Chaguo plotted a revolt but failed.

sentences.zh: 帝伐周，至詳古山，太后與帝祭文獻皇帝於行宮，群臣皆醉。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against Zhou, reached Xianggu Mountain, and the empress dowager and emperor sacrificed to Emperor Wenxian at the traveling palace; the assembled ministers were all drunk.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Zhou, the court reached Xianggu Mountain; the empress dowager and emperor offered sacrifice to Emperor Wenxian at the traveling palace, and the whole court was drunk.

sentences.zh: 察割歸見壽安王，邀與語，王弗從。

translations.literal: Chaguo returned and went to see Prince Shou'an, inviting him to speak; the prince would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo went to Prince Shou'an and asked to speak with him; the prince refused.

sentences.zh: 察割以謀告耶律盆都，盆都從之。

translations.literal: Chaguo disclosed the plot to Yelü Pendu, and Pendu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo revealed the plot to Yelü Pendu, who joined him.

sentences.zh: 是夕，同率兵入弒太后及帝，因僭位號。

translations.literal: That evening they together led troops in, murdered the empress dowager and the emperor, and thereupon usurped the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: That night they led their troops in and murdered the empress dowager and the emperor, then seized the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 百官不從者，執其家屬。

translations.literal: For officials who would not follow, they seized their families.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who refused to follow had their families seized as hostages.

sentences.zh: 至夜，閱內府物，見碼瑙碗，曰：「此希世寶，今為我有！」

translations.literal: At night he examined the objects of the inner treasury, saw an agate bowl, and said: "This is a treasure rare in the world—now it is mine!"
translations.idiomatic: That night he inspected the inner treasury, found an agate bowl, and exclaimed, "A treasure of the age—and now it is mine!"

sentences.zh: 詫於其妻。

translations.literal: He showed it to his wife in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He showed it proudly to his wife.

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「壽安王、屋質在，吾屬無噍類，此物何益！」

translations.literal: His wife said: "Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi are still alive—our kind will not leave a mouthful; what good is this object!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi are still alive—we shall not leave a soul alive; what good is this bowl!"

sentences.zh: 察割曰：「壽安年幼，屋質不過引數奴，詰旦來朝，固不足憂。」

translations.literal: Chaguo said: "Prince Shou'an is young, and Wuzhi is no more than a man leading a few slaves; at dawn they will come to court—surely there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo said, "Shou'an is young, and Wuzhi commands only a handful of slaves—they will come to court at dawn; there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 其黨矧斯報壽安、屋質以兵圍於外，察割尋遣人弒皇后於柩前，倉惶出陣。

translations.literal: His partisan Shengsi reported to Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi that troops had surrounded them outside; Chaguo soon sent men to murder the empress before the coffin, then rushed out in disarray to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Shengsi alerted Shou'an and Wuzhi that troops had surrounded them outside; Chaguo then sent men to murder the empress before the coffin and hurried out to give battle in confusion.

sentences.zh: 壽安遣人諭曰：「汝等既行弒逆，復將若何？」

translations.literal: Prince Shou'an sent someone to declare: "You have already committed regicide—what more do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shou'an sent a messenger to declare, "You have already murdered your sovereign—what do you plan to do next?"

sentences.zh: 有夷離堇劃者委兵歸壽安王，餘眾望之，徐徐而往。

translations.literal: An ürün chijin named Hua cast down his weapons and submitted to Prince Shou'an; the rest of the troops watched him and followed slowly.
translations.idiomatic: An ürün chijin named Hua laid down his arms and went over to Prince Shou'an; the rest of the troops watched him and drifted over one by one.

sentences.zh: 察割知其不濟，乃系群官家屬，執弓矢脅曰：「無過殺此曹爾！」

translations.literal: Chaguo knew he would not succeed; he bound the families of the assembled officials, seized bow and arrow, and threatened: "Nothing more than killing this lot!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he could not prevail, Chaguo bound the officials' families, took up bow and arrow, and threatened, "I need only kill this crowd!"

sentences.zh: 叱令速出。

translations.literal: He shouted, ordering them to hurry out.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted for them to come out at once.

sentences.zh: 時林牙耶律敵獵亦在系中，進曰：「不有所廢，壽安王何以興？

translations.literal: At the time the linya Yelü Dilie was also among those bound; he stepped forward and said: "Unless something is abolished, how can Prince Shou'an rise?
translations.idiomatic: Among those bound was the linya Yelü Dilie, who came forward and said, "Unless someone is removed, how can Prince Shou'an ascend the throne?

sentences.zh: 籍此為辭，猶可以免。」

translations.literal: Using this as your plea, you may still escape punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Use that as your plea and you may yet save yourselves."

sentences.zh: 察割曰：「誠如公言，誰當使者？」

translations.literal: Chaguo said: "If what you say is true, who shall be the envoy?"
translations.idiomatic: Chaguo said, "If you are right, who shall go as envoy?"

sentences.zh: 敵獵請與罨撒葛同往說之，察割從其計。

translations.literal: Dilie asked to go with Yansage to persuade them; Chaguo followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie offered to go with Yansage to negotiate; Chaguo agreed.

sentences.zh: 壽安王復令敵獵誘察割，臠殺之。

translations.literal: Prince Shou'an then had Dilie lure Chaguo out and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shou'an then had Dilie lure Chaguo out and had him hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: His sons were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 婁國，字勉辛，文獻皇帝之子。

translations.literal: Louguo, courtesy name Mianxin, was the son of Emperor Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Louguo, whose style name was Mianxin, was a son of Emperor Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 天祿五年，遙授武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianlu he was appointed Military Commissioner of Wuding in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianlu 5 he was appointed Military Commissioner of Wuding by remote commission.

sentences.zh: 及察割作亂，穆宗與屋質從林牙敵獵計，誘而出之，婁國手刃察割。

translations.literal: When Chaguo rebelled, Emperor Muzong and Wuzhi followed the linya Dili's plan to lure him out; Louguo personally slew Chaguo with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaguo rebelled, Muzong and Wuzhi adopted the linya Dili's stratagem to lure him out, and Louguo killed Chaguo with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 改南京留守。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as prefect of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 穆宗沈湎，不恤政事，婁國有覬覦之心，誘敵獵及群不逞謀逆。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong was sunk in drink and paid no heed to government; Louguo harbored designs of usurpation and incited Dilie and a group of unruly men to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong drowned himself in wine and neglected affairs of state; Louguo began to covet the throne and incited Dilie and other malcontents to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，按問不服。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, interrogation under torture yielded no confession.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, he was interrogated under torture but would not confess.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕為壽安王時，卿數以此事說我，今日豈有虛乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I was Prince Shou'an, you spoke of this matter many times—can there be falsehood today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I was still Prince Shou'an, you raised this very matter with me again and again—can it be empty talk today?"

sentences.zh: 婁國不能對。

translations.literal: Louguo could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Louguo had no answer.

sentences.zh: 及餘黨盡服，遂縊於可汗州西谷，詔有司擇絕後之地以葬。

translations.literal: When the remaining partisans had all submitted, he was strangled in the western valley of Kehan Prefecture; an edict ordered the relevant offices to choose a place cut off from posterity for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the remaining conspirators had submitted, he was strangled in the western valley of Kehan Prefecture, and an edict directed the authorities to choose a burial site that would cut off his line forever.

sentences.zh: 重元，小字孛吉只，聖宗次子。

translations.literal: Chongyuan, pet name Beijizhi, was the second son of Emperor Shengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyuan, whose childhood name was Beijizhi, was the second son of Emperor Shengzong.

sentences.zh: 材勇絕人，眉目秀朗，寡言笑，人望而畏。

translations.literal: His talent and courage surpassed others; his features were handsome and bright; he spoke little and laughed rarely; people feared him at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: His talent and bravery were unmatched; his face was handsome and clear; he spoke and laughed little, and men feared him at first sight.

sentences.zh: 太平三年，封秦國王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 聖宗崩，欽哀皇后稱制，密謀立重元。

translations.literal: When Shengzong died, Empress Dowager Qin'ai assumed regency and secretly plotted to establish Chongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Shengzong's death, Empress Dowager Qin'ai ruled as regent and secretly plotted to set Chongyuan on the throne.

sentences.zh: 重元以所謀白於上，上益重之，封為皇太弟。

translations.literal: Chongyuan disclosed the plot to the throne; the emperor esteemed him all the more and enfeoffed him as Imperial Younger Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyuan reported the plot to the emperor, who valued him all the more and enfeoffed him as Imperial Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 歷北院樞密使、南京留守、知元帥府事。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Commissioner of the Northern Commission, Prefect of Nanjing, and Director of the Marshal's Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Commissioner of the Northern Commission, Prefect of Nanjing, and Director of the Marshal's Bureau.

sentences.zh: 重元處戎職，未嘗離輦下。

translations.literal: Chongyuan held military office but never left the vicinity of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chongyuan held a military post, he never strayed far from the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 先是契丹人犯法，例須漢人禁勘，受枉者多。

translations.literal: Previously, when Khitan violated the law they had to be tried by Han officials, and many suffered injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Khitan broke the law they were tried by Han officials, and many were wronged.

sentences.zh: 重元奏請五京各置契丹警巡使，詔從之，賜以金券誓書。

translations.literal: Chongyuan memorialized requesting that each of the Five Capitals establish Khitan patrol commissioners; the edict approved it, and he was granted a golden certificate of pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyuan memorialized that each of the Five Capitals should have Khitan patrol commissioners; the court approved, and he was granted a golden pledge certificate.

sentences.zh: 道宗即位，冊為皇太叔，免拜不名，為天下兵馬大元帥，復賜金券、四頂帽、二色袍，尊寵所未有。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daozong took the throne, he was installed as Imperial Younger Uncle, exempted from bowing and from having his name spoken, made Grand Marshal of all armies and horses under Heaven, and again granted golden certificates, a four-peaked cap, and a two-colored robe—honors without precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Daozong ascended the throne, Chongyuan was made Imperial Younger Uncle, exempted from bowing and from having his name spoken aloud, appointed Grand Marshal of all armies under Heaven, and again given golden certificates, a four-peaked cap, and a two-colored robe—honors never granted before.

sentences.zh: 清寧九年，車駕獵灤水，以其子涅魯古素謀，與同黨陳國王陳六、知北院樞密事蕭胡睹等凡四百餘人，誘脅弩手軍陣於帷宮外。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning, when the imperial carriage hunted on the Luan River, relying on the longstanding plot of his son Nielugu together with the co-conspirator Prince of Chen Chen Liu, Commissioner of the Northern Commission Xiao Hudu, and more than four hundred others, they coerced the crossbow corps to form ranks outside the curtain palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingning 9, while the emperor hunted on the Luan River, Chongyuan—acting on the long-laid plot of his son Nielugu—joined Prince of Chen Chen Liu, Northern Commissioner Xiao Hudu, and more than four hundred others to coerce the crossbow troops into forming battle lines outside the curtain palace.

sentences.zh: 將戰，其黨多悔過效順，各自奔潰。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin, many of his partisans repented and submitted, each fleeing in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Just before battle, many of his followers repented and went over to the emperor, scattering in flight.

sentences.zh: 重元既知失計，北走大漠，嘆曰：「涅魯古使我至此！」

translations.literal: Chongyuan, knowing his plan had failed, fled north into the great desert and sighed: "Nielugu brought me to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Realizing his plan had failed, Chongyuan fled north into the desert and cried, "Nielugu has brought me to this pass!"

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 先是，重元將舉兵，帳前雨赤如血，識者謂敗亡之兆。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chongyuan was about to raise troops, before his tent rain fell red as blood; those who understood called it an omen of defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chongyuan was about to rebel, blood-red rain fell before his tent; those who read omens called it a sign of ruin.

sentences.zh: 子涅魯古。

translations.literal: His son Nielugu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Nielugu.

sentences.zh: 涅魯古，小字耶魯綰。

translations.literal: Nielugu, pet name Yeluwan.
translations.idiomatic: Nielugu, whose childhood name was Yeluwan.

sentences.zh: 性陰狠。

translations.literal: By nature he was secretive and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretive and ruthless by nature.

sentences.zh: 興宗一見，謂曰：「此子目有反相。」

translations.literal: At one sight Emperor Xingzong said: "This child's eyes bear the marks of rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: At first sight Emperor Xingzong said, "This boy's eyes bear the look of a rebel."

sentences.zh: 重熙十一年，封安定郡王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongxi he was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 11 he was made Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進王楚，為惕隱。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and made tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Prince of Chu and appointed tiyin.

sentences.zh: 清寧三年，出為武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingning he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingning 3 he was posted as Military Commissioner of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 七年，知南院樞密使事，說其父重元詐病，俟車駕臨問，因行弒逆。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Director of Southern Commission affairs; he urged his father Chongyuan to feign illness and wait for the imperial visit to inquire, then assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he took charge of Southern Commission affairs and urged his father Chongyuan to feign illness so that when the emperor came to inquire in person, they could strike.

sentences.zh: 九年秋獵，帝用耶律良之計，遣人急召涅魯古。

translations.literal: In the ninth year during the autumn hunt, the emperor followed Yelü Liang's plan and urgently summoned Nielugu.
translations.idiomatic: During the autumn hunt of the ninth year, the emperor adopted Yelü Liang's counsel and urgently summoned Nielugu.

sentences.zh: 涅魯古以事泄，遽擁兵犯行宮。

translations.literal: Nielugu, learning the affair was exposed, hastily gathered troops and attacked the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Nielugu learned the plot was exposed, he hastily raised troops and assaulted the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 南院樞密使許王仁先等率宿衛士討之。

translations.literal: The Southern Commission Director Prince Xu Renxian and others led the palace guards to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Commissioner Prince Xu Renxian and others led the palace guards against him.

sentences.zh: 涅魯古躍馬突出，為近侍詳穩渤海阿廝、護衛蘇射殺之。

translations.literal: Nielugu leaped his horse and rushed out; he was shot and killed by the close attendant commander Bohai Asi and guard Su.
translations.idiomatic: Nielugu spurred his horse and broke out of the line, but was shot down by the close attendant commander Bohai Asi and the guard Su.

sentences.zh: 滑哥，字斯懶，隋國王釋魯之子。

translations.literal: Huage, courtesy name Silan, was the son of Shilu, King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Huage, whose style name was Silan, was the son of Shilu, King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 性陰險。

translations.literal: By nature he was secretive and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretive and treacherous by nature.

sentences.zh: 初蒸其父妾，懼事彰，與克蕭臺哂等共害其父，歸咎臺哂，滑哥獲免。

translations.literal: At first he violated his father's concubine; fearing the affair would be exposed, together with Ke Xiao Taishan and others he jointly murdered his father, shifted the blame onto Taishan, and Huage escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He first violated his father's concubine; fearing exposure, he murdered his father with Ke Xiao Taishan and others, blamed Taishan, and Huage went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，務廣恩施，雖知滑哥凶逆，姑示含忍，授以惕隱。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor took the throne, he sought to extend grace widely; though he knew Huage was vicious and rebellious, for the moment he showed forbearance and appointed him tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he sought to extend favor broadly; though he knew Huage was vicious and rebellious, he temporarily showed forbearance and appointed him tiyin.

sentences.zh: 六年，滑哥預諸弟之亂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Huage took part in his younger brothers' rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Huage joined in his younger brothers' revolt.

sentences.zh: 事平，群臣議其罪，皆謂滑哥不可釋，於是與其子痕只俱淩遲而死，敕軍士恣取其產。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the assembled ministers deliberated on his crime; all said Huage must not be released; thereupon he and his son Henji were both executed by dismemberment, and an edict allowed soldiers to help themselves to his property freely.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, the ministers debated his crime; all agreed Huage could not be spared; he and his son Henji were then executed by dismemberment, and soldiers were permitted to seize his goods at will.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「滑哥不畏上天，反君弒父，其惡不可言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Huage does not fear Heaven above; he turned against his lord and murdered his father—his wickedness is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Huage fears neither Heaven nor his obligations; he rebelled against his lord and murdered his father—his wickedness is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 諸弟作亂，皆此人教之也。」

translations.literal: The rebellion of my younger brothers was all taught by this man."
translations.idiomatic: My younger brothers' rebellion was all instigated by this man."
